user.title: Security Monitor
user.description: Adds a Security Monitor panel to the sidebar (admins only) that shows access logs, token hygiene and outbound connections.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Security Monitor is already set up.

init.title: Advanced options
init.description:
**Exact hostnames for HTTP requests** shows the real hostname of every request made through Home Assistant's HTTP client. Without it, the Connections list shows names from DNS lookups or reverse DNS, and sometimes only an IP address.

⚠️ **Warning:** this replaces private methods of the aiohttp library for **all integrations**, not only this one. A future Home Assistant update that changes aiohttp could then break the HTTP requests of every integration. Only turn it on if you accept that risk, and turn it off first if integrations stop working after an update.

data.aiohttp_hostnames: Exact hostnames for HTTP requests (affects all integrations)

data_description.aiohttp_hostnames: Off by default. Saving reloads Security Monitor.

ip_ban_disabled.title: IP banning is disabled
ip_ban_disabled.description: Repeated failed logins are never blocked. Add `ip_ban_enabled: true` and `login_attempts_threshold` to the `http:` section of configuration.yaml.

external_http.title: Remote access without HTTPS
external_http.description: Your external URL uses plain HTTP, so passwords and tokens travel unencrypted. Use Home Assistant Cloud, a reverse proxy with TLS, or configure `ssl_certificate`.

stale_tokens.title: Unused long-lived access tokens
stale_tokens.description: Some long-lived access tokens haven't been used in 90 days. Revoke the ones you no longer need under your profile → Security.
